newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S. gas pipeline blasts pressure Canada prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gas pipeline blasts pressure Canada prices.

text.p: Two explosions on a pipeline that carries natural gas to U.S. markets from western Canada were forcing spot prices down sharply on Monday amid a glut of supply trapped in British Columbia, trading sources said.

Marketing sources said Westcoast Energy Inc's intra-B.C. system was packed up with gas on Monday after weekend blasts on Northwest Pipeline Corp, which interconnects with Westcoast at Sumas, Washington.
But a spokeswoman for Vancouver-based Westcoast said the company's system was running as normal on Monday and there were no cuts in firm or interruptible transportation service.
The ruptures occurred in Washington state on Saturday and Sunday. Northwest is a unit of Williams Cos Inc.

Traders pegged prices at Sumas at US$1.80 to US$1.90 per million British thermal units, but said that some deals had been discussed as low as US$1.50 per MmmBtu in early Monday trade. On Friday, Sumas was quoted at US$2.15/2.20 per mmBtu.

"It's dropping like a stone," said one Calgary-based trader, adding that many players were holding off on deals at Sumas and Westcoast's compressor station 2 until more details on Northwest were made available.

A Vancouver marketer said volumes into Northwest at Sumas were expected to be curtailed by 25 percent after the first blast, but it was not immediately known what effects the second incident would have.
Traders said the oversupply in British Columbia might also pressure prices in Alberta.
